answer: An agent market trading mesa surveys and pearl data can deter Sybil attacks using epoch-bound Verifiable Delay Functions, even when network fees hit a nadir. Each epoch, a randomness beacon seeds a sequential squaring proof tied to an agent's key, finished before a tight deadline yet rapidly verified. Faking identities requires concurrent single-thread cores and power per account, blocking precomputation. However, custom ASICs can outpace commodity CPUs to run several identities per chip.
